citation.authors: Maley MJ, Eglin CM, House JR, Tipton MJ

record.population: 10 Caucasian, 10 Asian and 10 men of African descent (AFD), UK laboratory
record.design: Controlled laboratory cooling of arm, hand (8 degrees C for 30 minutes) and foot in 30 degrees C air; skin blood flow and temperature measured
record.finding: Men of African descent had more intense and prolonged finger vasoconstriction during hand immersion than Caucasian men; skin blood flow during immersion was 24% (AFD) against 42% (Caucasian), and rewarming was slower (2.5 against 3.2 degrees C per minute). Cold sensation thresholds were similar. The authors note cold injuries are more prevalent in people of African descent and suggest this sensitivity may explain it.
record.note: Only 10 men of African descent, hands and feet, short laboratory exposures. This is physiology of cold response, not evidence about recovery or mood. 'Ethnicity' is the grouping used; the variable behind it was not measured.
